programme: STAT6, activated downstream of Th2/IL-4-IL-13 signalling, drives a SNAI1-dependent mesenchymal-transition programme (SNAI1's own target set includes CDH1, CDH3, CLDN1, CLDN3, VIM, ZEB1, MMP2 — the canonical loss-of-adhesion/gain-of-invasion signature), while NPAS2, a core circadian-clock factor (targets BMAL1, CRY1, CRY2, PER1, PER2), gates the timing of the stress/immune input that engages STAT6.
role_in_a: In IBS, STAT6-transduced IL-13 signalling degrades colonic epithelial barrier integrity, and NPAS2-linked circadian misalignment under stress co-occurs with gut dysfunction of the IBS type.
role_in_b: In lower grade glioma, STAT6 is epigenetically silenced, de-repressing HIF-1α-driven invasive growth, and IL4R/IL13/STAT6 pathway variants associate with glioma risk; SNAI1 operates through a miR-128-SP1 axis to drive glioma progression via an EMT-like transcriptional switch.
shared_axis: A Th2-cytokine-STAT6-SNAI1 'barrier-breakdown/mesenchymal-transition' module could plausibly be engaged both by a chronically stressed gut epithelium and by an invasive glioma margin, with NPAS2 supplying circadian gating on the IBS side; no retrieved paper states the two diseases share this axis, so the link rests on parallel single-disease evidence rather than a documented joint mechanism.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target lists and each carrying factor is independently placed in at least one of the two diseases by a direct citation, but nothing here documents IBS and glioma sharing this axis, and gut-vs-brain is not an obvious anatomical or clinical pairing, which is exactly the unexpected/moderate combination: coherent programme, undocumented cross-disease link, thin total evidence (six usable citations across three factors).
support: 38044939 (myrrh blocks IL-13-induced epithelial barrier breakdown in HT-29/B6 colonic cells, showing STAT6-axis engagement in a gut-barrier model); 22851040 (CD8+CD28 T-cell imbalance in ulcerative colitis, a related IBD phenotype, not IBS itself); 37404374 (glucocorticoid-receptor-mediated Nr1d1/circadian misalignment involving NPAS2 in stress-induced IBS-like gut dysfunction); 31530290 (epigenetic STAT6 downregulation raises HIF-1α, promoting glioma invasion); 21196282 (IL-4Ra/IL-13/STAT6 SNPs associate with brain glioma); 24959930 (SNAI1-miR-128-SP1 axis drives glioma/glioblastoma progression).
how_to_falsify: Stimulate IL-13/STAT6 signalling in a patient-derived IBS colonic organoid and separately in an LGG-derived glioma line; if SNAI1 induction and EMT markers (CDH1 loss, VIM/ZEB1 gain) do not track STAT6 activation in both systems, and NPAS2 knockdown does not alter the timing of the IL-13-STAT6 response in gut epithelium, the proposed shared module does not hold.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain vs colorectal, with only 2 independent cohort pairs behind the 124 patient-group comparisons, so replication is thinner than the comparison count suggests. RARA has direct glioma literature (RARA-AS1, 37833349) but is explicitly marked discordant between the two disease networks here, so it is excluded from the shared module rather than misrepresented as concordant. ARX has real IBS-relevant literature (enteroendocrine dysgenesis, 25171319) and the highest recurrence (69/124) but represents a distinct enteroendocrine-differentiation programme with no glioma evidence at all, so it is left out rather than forced into this story. POU4F2, CREBL2, BRCA1, YBX3, ERF, PITX3 and DLX3 had no disease-relevant literature retrieved (or clearly off-topic hits, e.g. ERF/rice-fibre, PITX3/head-and-neck cancer) and are excluded. The single-view list (CARF, MIXL1, COPS5, etc.) and tissue-generic list (FOXP3, EGR4, HDAC7, RFX5, STAT4) were checked and are not part of this account. STAT6's own OpenTargets signal is modest in IBS (percentile 0.21 of 2050) though stronger in LGG (percentile 0.72 of 589).
